name: Coding and STEM tuition
summary: How expat families evaluate coding, robotics, and STEM enrichment in Singapore — from after-school centres to competition tracks — without confusing weekend hobbies with school maths remediation.
body:
Singapore's enrichment market is dense with coding academies, robotics labs, and “future-ready” STEM brands. Expat parents usually want one of three things: a confidence-building hobby, a portfolio edge for international-school applications, or support that actually transfers into school maths/science — those goals need different providers.

## What good programmes clarify
- Age bands and prerequisite logic (scratch → Python, not random app badges)
- Class size, mentor-to-student ratio, and whether homework exists
- Competition pathways (NOI, robotics contests) versus project portfolios
- Device requirements and whether fees include hardware
- Make-up class and withdrawal terms during home-leave travel

Holiday camps are useful trials before annual contracts. Beware large prepaid packages sold at education fairs without a trial class.

## School alignment
International-school computer science and local-school maths olympiad prep are different products. If your child is struggling in classroom maths, a coding academy will not replace a maths tutor — and vice versa. Ask whether instructors can speak to your school's curriculum language (IB, IG, AP, MOE).

## Online vs in-centre
Online US/UK coding tutors can work across time zones; in-centre labs win for robotics hardware and peer energy. Hybrid models are common. Check PDPA-ish photo policies and whether sessions are recorded.

## How to choose
Prefer centres that show student project progression, publish instructor backgrounds, and let you observe a class. Avoid outfits that only market “AI certificates” for primary kids. For teens aiming at CS-heavy university paths, look for text-based programming depth and GitHub-style portfolios over drag-and-drop forever.

## Practical tip
Budget term fees beside CCA calendars and exam blocks. Many families over-commit enrichment in the first term after landing — start with one STEM slot until sleep and homework stabilise.
whenToEngage: When you want structured coding/robotics enrichment, a trial holiday camp, or STEM portfolio support that matches your child's school pathway — not as a substitute for core maths remediation.
